identity.title: ALMA Detections of CO Emission in the Most Luminous, Heavily Dust-obscured Quasars at z > 3

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report the results of a pilot study of CO$(4-3)$ emission line of three *WISE*-selected hyper-luminous, dust-obscured quasars (QSOs) with sensitive ALMA Band 3 observations.

distance_source.value: optical redshift from Wu et al. 2012; CO redshift from Gaussian fits

question.value: What are the molecular gas properties and kinematics (merger or outflow signatures) of three WISE-selected hyper-luminous obscured QSOs at z>3, and do they follow the L'CO-LFIR relation of unobscured QSOs?

evidence.quote: Our purpose is to study the molecular gas properties and search the clues for feeding and feedback processes in the most luminous obscured QSOs.
ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.01148.S (PI: Lulu Fan)
Observations were carried out with ALMA during Cycle 3 using the Band 3 receiver.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: One spectral window on redshifted CO(4-3) (line mode, centres 109.054, 109.998, 100.393 GHz); three other spectral windows in continuum mode

evidence.quote: The spectral window of the redshifted CO$(4-3)$ line used a setup for spectral line mode, while the three remaining spectral windows used a continuum mode setup.
For each source, the receiver was tuned to the redshifted CO$(4-3)$ line using the optical redshift taken from (cite: wu2012).
The telescope configuration included baselines between 15 and 1124 m (though 1396 m for W0149+2350).
The angular resolution is 0.2 arcsec, which corresponds to $\sim$1.5 kpc at $z\sim3.2$.
In the line spectral window, the rms is $\sim0.59$ mJy/beam per 21.5 km s$^{-1}$ channel.

findings_qualitative.value: All three QSOs show complex CO velocity structures disfavoring a rotating disk

evidence.quote: The PV-diagrams also suggest that all of three QSOs have complex velocity structures, which may disfavor the scenario of rotation disk.

findings_qualitative.value: No serendipitous continuum or CO companions in the Band 3 FOV

evidence.quote: we have not found any serendipitous detection of dust continuum or CO emission line around our obscured QSOs

claims.hypothesis: Obscured hyper-luminous QSOs at z>3 are gas-rich
claims.experiment: CO(4-3) detection and conversion to Mgas

evidence.quote: The total gas masses range from $10^{10}$ to $10^{11}$ M$_\odot$, suggesting that these QSOs are gas-rich systems.

claims.hypothesis: Obscured QSOs follow the L'CO-LFIR relation of unobscured QSOs
claims.finding: Possibly similar objects at different evolutionary stages

evidence.quote: We find that the three dust-obscured QSOs follow the similar $L'_{\rm CO}- L_{\rm FIR}$ relation as unobscured QSOs at high redshifts.

claims.hypothesis: CO kinematics indicate merger or outflow
claims.experiment: Multi-Gaussian line fits and PV diagrams
claims.result: Three components in W0149; double Gaussian in other two
claims.finding: Possible merger in W0149+2350; possible outflows in W0220+0137 and W0410-0913

evidence.quote: The possibility that they are just a single Gaussian component can not be fully excluded.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Merger vs outflow interpretations cannot be fully distinguished

evidence.quote: though the scenario of having a molecular outflow can not be excluded

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample and limited S/N for double-Gaussian preference; W0410 line truncated at band edge

evidence.quote: despite the choice is not as convincing as for W0149+2350 due to the limited signal-to-noise
